storySections.title: Basic Information
storySections.content:
Everyone wears a mask; she chose the one that numbs the heart best—

She smiles gently, she speaks gently, and every look and every word lands exactly where it needs to, until the patients who come to her for counseling believe with all their hearts that they have found the one person who understands them, the one who will show them the way.
That is enough.

A moth doomed to burn does not need to know how it ends. It only needs to keep following where she leads.

And inside that warmth that looks so much like salvation, the fire takes hold, and there is no turning back.

storySections.title: Story: I
storySections.content:
I don't believe Robert put a gun in his mouth. No. I don't believe it.
He was decorated for valor. He closed murder cases nobody else could crack. He was a veteran agent with an iron will. And he was getting married soon—the two of them loved each other. So there has to be something behind this. Someone killed him and dressed it up as a suicide.
Whoever did it, I will find them, and I will make them pay. I owe him that as his brother, and as an agent.
...
The scene gave me nothing, so I came back to our hometown—the last place Robert went before he died. After asking around, I learned he had gone up into the mountains.
As for why, I suspect it has to do with the local custom: every family's firstborn is taken into the mountains by their parents for the coming-of-age rite.
Our parents moved away when we were still children, so Robert never went through it. I think the weight of starting a family of his own woke some old sense of obligation in him.
Either way, I'm going up there. I set out the moment I finish writing this.
...
There is a vast structure cut into the mountain. I can't tell what age it belongs to. I can't tell anything about it. All I know is that the rituals here have never once stopped. The severed limbs, the pupae—ugh. I can't write any more.
...
These pupae... no. No. That isn't my grandmother, my grandfather, the people my family came from... I can't have a monster's blood in me. Aaah—
...
...The monsters at the ritual have found me. They mean to make me one of them!
...
If anyone finds this, kill me. Now, right now...@2
...
Praise be to great @2, hssss @2... praise the blind and idiot @4... hss hss hss... @1 hssss...
—Excerpted, with omissions, from the diary of the late Agent @3

storySections.title: Story: II
storySections.content:
"Thank you, Clementine. I feel so much better. You understand me better than anyone in the world."
The Keeper hears something like that almost every time they pass Clementine's counseling room. However the patients and Awakeners look going in, they come out light on their feet and smiling.
Once, walking by, the Keeper even caught her counseling a stray cat that had wandered in by mistake.
The results speak for themselves. Everyone who sits down with her comes away singing her praises, and her influence spreads fast. It also brings complications—
"Good afternoon, Keeper."
Clementine is waiting with a smile on the one road you have to take, and you aren't surprised. That communicator of hers, ringing and ringing, says everything. Her patients trust her completely, and somewhere along the way they became her eyes and ears, helping her get what she wants, one way or another.
"I'd wager that if you decided to run this city, your patients would hand you the mayor's chair without asking a single question."
Clementine only smiles the joke away.
"None of that interests me."
And it truly doesn't. Which is a mercy.
Otherwise the dark little things confessed in that room would be enough to tear the city apart.
"For now, the only secrets I want are the ones buried deepest in you, Keeper."

storySections.title: Story: III
storySections.content:
The truth is that the real Clementine died the instant that great, long-dead will took her as its host.
What broke from the cocoon on that altar of blood and torn flesh was something newborn—great in essence, far beyond any human life.
A new life with old memories. A body grown on this planet, a soul born in the depths of the universe.
The contradiction bewildered her, but not for long. The hunger in that soul soon left no room for thought.
Human food was tasteless. Only memories of suffering went down at all, and the more torment and despair they held, the sweeter they were.
That was the moment she understood how she was meant to live.
"Tell me. The pain, the despair—show me all of it."
She sat behind her desk, watching each patient with pure malice, her face so gentle that anyone would lower their guard.
Camouflage. The mask an insect wears when it hunts.

storySections.title: Story: IV
storySections.content:
At first the smallest scraps of suffering were enough for her.
Then the craving for something sweeter began to seep into her sessions, a little more malice folded in each time.
It gathered like a river and broke its banks, and it drowned one island of a mind after another.
And still it wasn't enough. Nowhere near enough.
Only when that ancient dream wakes will the whole world become an ocean of pain, and the joy of it be complete.
So she burns, she prays, she waits.
When everything falls into chaos, she will bow her head and savor the purest grief this world can offer.
Even if that ocean drowns her too.

daily.title: Awaken
daily.content: Forgive my intrusion, I simply sensed a low psychological energy and came to check on you. Now, Keeper, shall we embark on a journey through your mind?

daily.title: Upgrade: I
daily.content: If you seek my thoughts, you may be disappointed. I'm better at listening than I am at offering commentary.

daily.title: Upgrade: II
daily.content: Ah, I heard His voice... those murmurs, every syllable filled with the utmost agony.

daily.title: Upgrade: III
daily.content: I will remember the pain of this moment... recalling and savoring it again and again.

daily.title: Enlighten: Observe
daily.content: Psychiatrists once cured patients by drilling open their skulls with a trepanation technique... Please, relax. That was long ago. We have since developed far more methods to delve into the mind.

daily.title: Enlighten: Ponder
daily.content: First, let's listen to some music. How do you like this melody? Soothing and gentle. Now, let your body and mind resonate with the music, entering a state of spiritual relaxation.

daily.title: Enlighten: Reflect
daily.content: Your vision is probably filled with bizarre hallucinations now, which is quite normal. Draw them out, and your subconscious and instincts will reveal everything.

daily.title: Enlighten: Insight
daily.content: Next is Philip Pinel's moral therapy. You must express your innermost desires and fears. It's a necessary procedure to unshackle the mind and restore dormant humanity.

daily.title: Enlighten: Elevate
daily.content: Remember those fears, detail your feelings of pain. The essence of emotional impact therapy is to face pain directly and conquer it. Here, I'll wipe away your tears. Take your time. Tell me those memories in detail...

daily.title: Enlighten: Florish
daily.content: Congratulations, you have been healed. Yes, those hallucinations and illusions are normal; they are proof of your recovery.

daily.title: Affinity: I
daily.content: Weavers, lawyers, barons... I'll never turn a patient away for a fee. To me, they are all merely patients in need of healing.

daily.title: Affinity: II
daily.content: Poor Mr. White. His family kept him in a pigpen because asylums in the neighborhood were full. I treated him for free, and after that, he finally realized he was a person, not livestock. He then reclaimed his dignity, with his own hands.

daily.title: Affinity: III
daily.content: Hydrotherapy, electroconvulsive therapy, restraining therapy... those are not treatments, but torture. So, I've been treating the patients in those hospitals my way, pro bono. Eventually, they all achieved recovery and found true freedom.

daily.title: Affinity: IV
daily.content: These patients have given me beautiful memories. Next, it's your turn, Keeper. I've already chosen a perfect ending for you. It will be the most exquisite consultation of my career.

daily.title: Affinity: V
daily.content: I admit I underestimated you. Your existence is pain itself. This time, there's no need for follow-up visits. I want to stay by your side and see the outcome firsthand.

daily.title: Chat: Touch
daily.content: To understand each other, one must open their heart. Touch here, and my silver heart will open for you.

daily.title: Chat: About the Crisis
daily.content: Mental illness is not exclusive to this era; it transcends time and space. Dissolution is the same. Both transcend the boundaries of human cognition, don't they?

daily.title: Chat: About Mythag
daily.content: This place is filled with traces of history, and to some extent, history represents memories... painful memories of the departed.

daily.title: Chat: What I Like
daily.content: A dark room, all alone, along with the countless painful whispers constantly echoing in my mind... this is the best way to enjoy time.

daily.title: Chat: What I Hate
daily.content: A numb soul holds no interest for me. Their souls are already dead. No matter how much one stirs them, there will not be a ripple.

daily.title: Chat: About the Keeper
daily.content: As a fragment of that existence, you carry Their scent... A beautiful scent, filled with pain. It makes any memory of yours taste incredibly delicious.

daily.title: Chat: About Aurita
daily.content: Though it may be impolite to say, talking to that child only bores me. You can only ever see one expression... a smile.

daily.title: Chat: About Aigis
daily.content: Aigis looks much brighter now. Of course, if my little guest needs help, I'm happy to offer it. I mean, genuine help.

daily.title: Chat: About Psychological Analysis
daily.content: Keeper, can you help me with a small test? The Rorschach inkblot test. It will help me see the depths of your inner self... I will become the only Awakener to unveil the secrets of your heart.

battle.title: Investigation Begins
battle.content: No need for such nervousness. This is merely a regular consultation.

battle.title: Investigation Success
battle.content: Pain, despair, death... these memories taste like dessert after a fine meal.

battle.title: Investigation Halted
battle.content: Refusing a doctor's help will not benefit you. Perhaps next time, we'll try deep hypnosis.

battle.title: Skill: II
battle.content: I will savor this sweet pain.

battle.title: Rouse
battle.content: Watch the pendulum... follow its movement with your eyes.

battle.title: Exalt
battle.content: Shh... quiet. Now, walk toward the ending I'll guide you to.

battle.title: Over-Exalt
battle.content: Don't be shy, there's no need to hide. I am your sole confidante. Come, pour out your deepest pain to me.
